THE SECOND PRESBYTERIAN ROLL — A NAME ON A CHURCH LIST THAT OPENS IN 1842, AND NEVER AN 1835 FACT. The 1892 printed membership roll of the Second Presbyterian Church of Chicago, read line by line into this repository, carries 1 line whose surname and given initial agree with this person's — “Bradford, William J. | Letter. | December 28, 1887. | Dismissed.” (second_presb_0432, printed page 179), admitted 1887-12-28 by letter. persons.note: THE LADDER'S OWN READING OF THIS EVIDENCE. Read from newspaper_letter_list, poll_1834. THE GRADE IS THE OWNER'S RATIFIED LADDER OF 2026-09-03 (G1c), applied to every identity at once by tools/consolidate_resident_evidence.py and spent onto this card by tools/mint_civic_residents.py; the evidence blocks below carry the reading AS READ, its locator and the record it came from, so the page can be gone back to. THE TOWN'S OWN ROLLS, 1833-1835 — CORROBORATION, NOT A GRADE. The early Chicago voter and tax lists held by the Illinois Regional Archives Depository name this person 1 time: Election returns — poll list of 1834, filed 11 August 1834 — “Knight, Clark” (poll_1834_069, line 238). These are the town's own contemporary paper rather than a recollection of it, and each appearance says that a man of that name stood on that roll in that year — no more. The reading is twice mediated (Schulz's transcription, then Genealogy Trails' republication) and this project has not seen the IRAD originals. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) the 1835 poll with a second independent source is attested, the 1835 poll alone or a 1833/1834 list with another source is inferred, and a single appearance with nothing else is a projected resident. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE — T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: one resident of the surname 'Knight' agrees with the entry's forenames; 2 bearer(s) of the surname were considered. (data/research/civic/voter_crosswalk.json).

A scan read that confirms or corrects the name upgrades this entry. OLD SETTLERS, 1879 — A DATE THIS MAN GAVE FOR HIMSELF, AND STILL NOT A FACT ABOUT 1835. The Calumet Club's FIRST reception to the settlers of Chicago prior to 1840, 27 May 1879, printed its register in the proceedings (Early Chicago, Chicago, 1879, pages 84-90), and this man's entry reads “Marshall, James A. | 1832, | London, Eng. | 70 | Chicago.” — name, his own date of arrival, his birthplace, his age and his 1879 post-office address, in the register's five columns. The date of arrival is HIS RECOLLECTION, set down forty to sixty years after the event; the address is where he lived in 1879 and is never read as an 1835 residence. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a later recollection corroborates, enriches and dates and cannot lift a rung by itself, so this record's GRADE IS UNCHANGED by it: T-0513 consolidates the identity and T-0515 regrades. Identity by rule OS2A — one bearer of the surname, the forename initial agrees, and the resident's own record spells the roster's forename 'james' — the discriminator the roster's initials do not supply (data/research/old_settlers/crosswalk.json). OLD SETTLERS, 1882 — CORROBORATION, NOT A NEW FACT ABOUT 1835. The Calumet Club's fourth annual reception to the settlers of Chicago prior to 1840, held 18 May 1882, printed this man among the guests present as “Marshall, James A., 2906 Indiana avenue, Chicago.” (Chicago Tribune, 19 May 1882). The club's criterion was residence in Chicago before 1 January 1840 and majority by then: the roster therefore corroborates a pre-1840 Chicago residence and says he was alive in 1882. It gives NO year of arrival, and the address it prints is where he lived in 1882, forty-seven years after the scene date — it is not an 1835 residence and is not read as one. persons.name: Giles Spring
persons.note: HIS FIRST OFFICE WAS A BARREL-HEAD AND HIS SECOND WAS DESK-ROOM IN CATON'S. The two of them opposed each other in the first larceny case heard before a justice of the peace in July 1833, and Caton's account of hiring out to carry the chain for a surveyor on the North Side that same month - because clients were few, fees small and board bills maturing - is the only description in this dataset of what an educated newcomer actually did for money in the town's first summer. THE TOWN'S OWN ROLLS, 1833-1835 — CORROBORATION, NOT A GRADE. The early Chicago voter and tax lists held by the Illinois Regional Archives Depository name this person 2 times: Election returns — poll list of 1834, filed 11 August 1834 — “Spring, Giles” (poll_1834_103, line 272); Poll list of 1835 — “Spring, G.” (poll_1835_075, line 362). These are the town's own contemporary paper rather than a recollection of it, and each appearance says that a man of that name stood on that roll in that year — no more. The reading is twice mediated (Schulz's transcription, then Genealogy Trails' republication) and this project has not seen the IRAD originals. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) the 1835 poll with a second independent source is attested, the 1835 poll alone or a 1833/1834 list with another source is inferred, and a single appearance with nothing else is a projected resident. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE — T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: one resident of the surname 'Spring' agrees with the entry's forenames; 1 bearer(s) of the surname were considered. (data/research/civic/voter_crosswalk.json). THE FEDERAL LAND TRACT SALES — A PURCHASE, AND NEVER A RESIDENCE. The Illinois State Archives' Public Domain Land Tract Sales register enters this person 3 times, as “SPRING GILES”, 1836-06-29 to 1836-09-05: 3 lots in the platted town — lot 4 of block 41 in the town the register codes CHIOT (L4BL41CHIOT, as printed); lot 5 of block 12 in the town the register codes CHIOTV (L5BL12CHIOTV, as printed); lot 6 of block 12 in the town the register codes CHIOTV (L6BL12CHIOTV, as printed), 0.00 acres stated in all, for $5850.00 (ls1465, ls1466, ls1467). THE REGISTER'S OWN RESIDENCE COLUMN READS UNKNOWN on these rows: a county, a state or nothing, and never a town, which is why a purchase here places nobody. THE TOWN LOTS ARE THE PLAT ITSELF, AND THEY ARE NOT ACRES: Cook County's register describes them by lot and block in a platted town and gives them no section, no township and no acreage at all, so they add nothing to the acre figure above and $5850.00 to the money. This project does not expand the register's town codes, so which addition a lot stands in is carried as the code and not as a name. It is still a purchase and it still places nobody. A purchase and nothing more. It dates and places a transaction; it proposes no residence, and under the ratified ladder it corroborates rather than mints. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: SPRING GILES matches Giles Spring: the forename names Giles Spring of the 1 person of this surname, and the forename agrees in full. (data/research/land_sales/resident_crosswalk.json). This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a second independent source is what lifts a projected resident, and a land entry is a second source about a TRANSACTION rather than about who was living at Chicago on 1 July 1835 — a man may buy a quarter-section he never sees. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict.

Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a second independent source is what lifts a projected resident, and a land entry is a second source about a TRANSACTION rather than about who was living at Chicago on 1 July 1835 — a man may buy a quarter-section he never sees. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict.

residents.research_note: MINTED FROM THE LETTER LISTS (T-0378, T-0379). THE HOUSEHOLD IS A CONTAINER, NOT AN ARGUMENT: every other record here argues for a household, and this one argues for a PERSON. `data/residents/` cannot carry a person outside a household, so one was written around them and told to claim nothing — one member, no dwelling, no division, no trade, no family, no arrival beyond the paper's bound. tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py derives the set and prints every refusal, `--gate` proves no record here gained a roof, a trade or a second member, and docs/LIBERTIES.md L214 carries the change of scale.

research_note: RECONSTRUCTED / GENERATED, NOT AN ATTESTED NAMED BUILDING. The block, its scheduled roof count and its family mix follow the 665-roof programme; exact presence, lot, position, footprint, finish and instance-level form are interpretive. H-family house massing currently resolves through the frame dwelling archetype; no larger house generator is implemented. THE CENTRE HALL IS THE ENTRY'S, NOT THIS PARCEL'S (T-1686). H1 is the only family of the thirty-five whose crosswalk entry names a centre hall and states a bare bay count — its required variant is "center_hall_one_and_half" and its variants line reads "5 bays; center hall; kitchen ell; small porch" — so the plan and the bay count below are read off that entry and not dealt by this parcel. The kitchen ell and the small porch the same line offers are NOT raised with them: both are selectable variants beside the required one, and an ell is a footprint fact this record's rectangle does not carry.
